leadText: The following is a list of all of the English language home video releases of the Pokémon movies in and . DVD releases are for , releases are for (although they may be playable in other regions), and all releases are .
plainText:
The following is a list of all of the English language home video releases of the Pokémon movies in and . DVD releases are for , releases are for (although they may be playable in other regions), and all releases are .

==Single movie releases==
===Mewtwo Strikes Back===
Pokémon: The First Movie - Mewtwo Strikes Back was initially released on home video in Australia by Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Pikachu's Vacation. The promotional card was included in early releases of the DVD. It was released on VHS in Australia with the catalogue number 18270. It was released on DVD in Australia with the catalogue number DVS18270. These releases use a 4:3 .

The DVD has English, French, Italian, Dutch, and Portuguese audio; with optional English, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, English for the hearing impaired, and Italian for the hearing impaired closed captions. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Commentary audio track by Director Michael Haigney and Producer Norman J. Grossfeld
The Story of Mewtwo's Origin (first two minutes of The Uncut Story of Mewtwo's Origin)
Music video for 's " " (the movie's ending theme)
Theatrical trailer of the movie
Preview of The Power of One
"Ash's Journey"
DVD-ROM features 

The VHS had The Story of Mewtwo's Origin (first two minutes of The Uncut Story of Mewtwo's Origin) added to the beginning of the film.

It was re-released on DVD in a Collector's Edition Tin in Australia and New Zealand by on December 2, 2015 with the catalogue number BHE6417. It was released on DVD in standard case by Beyond Home Entertainment in Australia on February 3, 2016 and in New Zealand on February 17, 2016 with the catalogue number BHE6679. These releases do not include a Pikachu short or any other special features. These releases use a .

It was re-released once again by Shock Entertainment in Australia on February 3, 2021 and in New Zealand on March 24, 2021 with an updated cover and the catalogue number KAL5556B.

 

===The Power of One===
 
Pokémon: The Movie 2000 - The Power of One was initially released on home video in Australia by Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Pikachu's Rescue Adventure. It was released on VHS in Australia with the catalogue number 18620. It was released on a double-sided DVD in Australia with the catalogue number DVS18620. The DVD release uses a 1.85:1 . The DVD has English, French, and Italian audio; with optional English, French, Italian, Dutch, Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Italian for the hearing impaired, and English for the hearing impaired closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Musical performances from the Pokémon the Movie 2000 soundtrack
"They Don't Understand" by 
"Story Of" and performance by Alysha Antonino
"Pokémon World" by featuring 
Making of the soundtrack
Theatrical trailer of the movie
Theatrical trailer of Spell of the Unown: Entei

It was re-released on DVD in a Collector's Edition Tin in Australia and New Zealand by on December 2, 2015 with the catalogue number BHE6418. It was released on DVD in standard case by Beyond Home Entertainment in Australia on February 3, 2016 and in New Zealand on February 17, 2016 with the catalogue number BHE6680. These releases do not include a Pikachu short or any other special features. These releases use a aspect ratio.

It was re-released once again by Shock Entertainment in Australia on February 3, 2021 and in New Zealand on March 24, 2021 with a different cover and the catalogue number KAL5557B.

 

===Spell of the Unown: Entei===
 
Spell of the Unown: Entei was initially released on home video in Australia by Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Pikachu & Pichu. It was released on VHS in Australia with the catalogue number 21101. It was released on a double-sided DVD in Australia with the catalogue number DVS21251. The DVD release uses a 1.85:1 . The DVD has English, French, Italian, Dutch, Hebrew, and Greek audio; with English, French, Italian, Dutch, Greek, Hebrew, English for the hearing impaired, and Italian for the hearing impaired closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Pokérap GS (Johto Pokérap)
Making of "To Know the Unknown"
"The Filmmakers Say" (audio commentary)
Theatrical trailer of the movie

It was re-released on DVD in a Collector's Edition Tin in Australia and New Zealand by on December 2, 2015 with the catalogue number BHE6419. It was released on DVD in standard case by Beyond Home Entertainment in Australia on February 3, 2016 and in New Zealand on February 17, 2016 with the catalogue number BHE6681. These releases do not include a Pikachu short or any other special features. These releases use a aspect ratio.

It was re-released once again by Shock Entertainment in Australia on February 3, 2021 and in New Zealand on March 24, 2021 with an updated cover and the catalogue number KAL5558B.

 

===Celebi: The Voice of the Forest===
 
Celebi: The Voice of the Forest was released on home video in Australia by .

It was initially published by Miramax and distributed by on VHS and DVD. It was released on VHS in Australia with the catalogue number B15360. It was released on DVD in Australia with the catalogue number E15360. The cover states that it includes an exclusive Pokémon short; of which such a thing is not included. Buena Vista stated that this was a mistake and later reprints of the cover removed the mention of the short. The DVD release uses a . The DVD has English and German audio, with English (for the hearing impaired) and German closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Audio commentary by the actors and producers
Multi-angle animation progression on four scenes
Pokémon 4Ever trivia game
English and Japanese theatrical trailers for the movie
Japanese theatrical trailer for Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias

It was re-released again on DVD with the catalogue number C-124714-9 in Australia and New Zealand on November 9, 2016, this time distributed by (as ) and published by . This release uses a 4:3 aspect ratio.

 

===Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias===
 
Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias was released on home video in Australia by .

It was initially published by Miramax and distributed by on VHS and DVD. Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Camp Pikachu. It was released on VHS in Australia with the catalogue number B16060. It was released on DVD in Australia with the catalogue number E16060. The DVD release uses a 4:3 . The DVD has English, French, and Spanish audio; with English (for the hearing impaired), French, and Spanish closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Location scouting in Venice
An animation stages feature (Water Chariot Race, Race Spectators, Crowd on a Bridge, Latias, Defense Mechanism of Alto Mare, Wave)
The characters of the movie
Pokémon Heroes trivia game

It was released again on DVD with the catalogue number C-124715-9 in Australia and New Zealand on November 9, 2016, this time distributed by (as ) and published by . This release uses a 4:3 aspect ratio.

 

===Jirachi: Wish Maker===
Jirachi: Wish Maker was published by and distributed by (as ) on DVD in Australia and New Zealand. It was released on DVD in Australia and New Zealand on November 9, 2016 with the catalogue number is C-124716-9. This release uses a .

 

===Destiny Deoxys===
Destiny Deoxys was published by and distributed by (as ) on DVD in Australia and New Zealand. It was released on DVD in Australia and New Zealand on November 9, 2016 with the catalogue number is C-124717-9. This release uses a .

 

===Lucario and the Mystery of Mew===
Lucario and the Mystery of Mew was released by (now known as Beyond Home Entertainment) on DVD in Australia on August 16, 2006 and in New Zealand on November 7, 2007. Its catalogue number is 12440. This release uses a .

This movie was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7426 on November 16, 2016 in Australia. This release uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

This move was re-released by Shock Entertainment in Australia on June 2, 2021 with an updated cover and the catalogue number KAL5633B.

 

===Pokémon Ranger and the Temple of the Sea===
Pokémon Ranger and the Temple of the Sea was released by (now known as Beyond Home Entertainment) on DVD in Australia on February 6, 2008 and in New Zealand on March 5, 2008. Its catalogue number is 12722. This release uses a .

This movie was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7427 on November 16, 2016 in Australia. This release uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

This movie was re-released by Shock Entertainment in Australia on June 2, 2021 with an updated cover and the catalogue number KAL5634B.

 

===The Rise of Darkrai===
The Rise of Darkrai was released by (now known as Beyond Home Entertainment) on DVD in Australia on November 5, 2008 and in New Zealand on April 1, 2011. Its catalogue number is 12921. This release uses a .

This movie was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7428 on November 16, 2016 in Australia. This release uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

This movie was re-released by Shock Entertainment in Australia on April 6, 2022 with an updated cover and the catalogue number KAL5635.

 

===Giratina and the Sky Warrior===
Giratina and the Sky Warrior was released by (now known as Beyond Home Entertainment) on DVD in Australia on June 3, 2009 and in New Zealand on August 7, 2009. Its catalogue number is 13086. This release uses a .

This movie was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7429 on November 16, 2016 in Australia. This release uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

This movie was re-released by Shock Entertainment in Australia on April 6, 2022 with an updated cover and the catalogue number KAL5636.

 

===Arceus and the Jewel of Life===
Arceus and the Jewel of Life was released by (now known as Beyond Home Entertainment) in Australia.

It was released on DVD by Magna Home Entertainment with the catalogue number 13347 in Australia on June 2, 2010 and in New Zealand on October 8, 2010. It was released on Blu-ray by Magna Home Entertainment with the catalogue number BD13698 in Australia on June 1, 2011 and in New Zealand on June 16, 2011. These releases use a .

This movie was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7430 on November 16, 2016 in Australia. This release uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

This movie was re-released by Shock Entertainment in Australia on April 6, 2022 with an updated cover and the catalogue number KAL5637.

 

===Zoroark: Master of Illusions===
Zoroark: Master of Illusions was released by (now known as Beyond Home Entertainment) on home video in Australia. The promotional card was included in early releases of both the DVD and the Blu-ray (marked with a sticker to indicate the presence of the card).

It was released on DVD in Australia on June 1, 2011 with the catalogue number 13732. It was released on Blu-ray in Australia on June 1, 2011 and in New Zealand on June 16, 2011 . The DVD release uses a while the Blu-ray release uses a 1.85:1 aspect ratio.

This movie was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7431 on November 16, 2016 in Australia. This release uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

 

===White—Victini and Zekrom and Black—Victini and Reshiram===
White—Victini and Zekrom and Black—Victini and Reshiram were both released by (now known as Beyond Home Entertainment) on DVD in Australia on March 7, 2012 and in New Zealand on March 8, 2012. White has the catalogue number 13957 and Black has the catalogue number 13958. These releases use a .

Promotional cards were included in early releases of both DVDs. was included with White and was included with Black. They were marked with a sticker to indicate the presence of the card.

 

===Kyurem VS. The Sword of Justice===
Kyurem VS. The Sword of Justice was released by on home video in Australia. The promotional card was included in early releases of both the DVD and the Blu-ray (marked with a sticker to indicate the presence of the card). All of the releases use a .

It was released on DVD with the catalogue number BHE4677 in Australia on March 6, 2013 and in New Zealand on March 20, 2013. It was released on Blu-ray in Australia on March 6, 2013 and in New Zealand on March 20, 2013.

Special Collector's Editions for both the DVD and the Blu-ray were released in Australia and New Zealand on the same day as the standard release, exclusive to . This Digipack includes exclusive artwork on the inside of the cover. The Keldeo TCG card was also included in these releases.

A special edition including a Keldeo figure was released with the catalogue number BHE4747 in Australia on June 5, 2013.

This movie was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7433 on November 16, 2016 in Australia.

Standard Editions
 

Special Editions
 

===Genesect and The Legend Awakened===
Genesect and The Legend Awakened was released by on DVD in Australia on December 4, 2013 and in New Zealand on December 6, 2013. Its catalogue number is BHE5161. This release uses a . 

This movie was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7434 on November 16, 2016 in Australia. This release uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

 

===Diancie and the Cocoon of Destruction===
Diancie and the Cocoon of Destruction was released by on DVD in Australia on December 3, 2014 and in New Zealand on December 10, 2014. Its catalogue number is BHE5775. This release uses a .

This movie was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7435 on November 16, 2016 in Australia. This release uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

 

===Hoopa and the Clash of Ages===
Hoopa and the Clash of Ages was released by on DVD in Australia on December 2, 2015. Its catalogue number is BHE6524. This release uses a .

This movie was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7436 on November 16, 2016 in Australia. This release uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

 

===Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel===
Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel was released by on DVD in Australia on December 7, 2016 and in New Zealand on December 1, 2016. Its catalogue number is BHE7529. This release uses a .

 

===I Choose You!===
I Choose You! was released by in Australia and New Zealand.

It was released on DVD with the catalogue number BHE7777 in Australia on December 6, 2017 and in New Zealand on December 13, 2017. It was released on Blu-ray with the catalogue number BHE7787BR in Australia on December 6, 2017 and in New Zealand on October 17, 2018. This release uses a . The Blu-ray release is exclusive to .

 

===The Power of Us===
The Power of Us was released by in Australia and New Zealand.

It was released on DVD with the catalogue number BHE8000 in Australia on December 5, 2018 and in New Zealand on December 12, 2018. It was released on Blu-ray with the catalogue number BHE8035BR in Australia on December 5, 2018 and in New Zealand on December 12, 2018. This release uses a .

This movie was released on DVD and Blu-ray by Beyond Home Entertainment with alternate artwork exclusively at stores in Australia on December 12, 2018. It has the catalogue number BHE8032 on DVD and BHE8033BR on Blu-ray. These releases use a 16:9 aspect ratio.

 

===Mewtwo Strikes Back—Evolution===
Mewtwo Strikes Back—Evolution was released by Shock Entertainment in Australia and New Zealand.

It was released on DVD in Australia on March 3, 2021 and in New Zealand on May 19, 2021 with the catalogue number KAL5523B and on Blu-ray in Australia on March 3, 2021 and in New Zealand on May 19, 2021 with the catalogue number KAL5523B.

 

===Secrets of the Jungle===
Secrets of the Jungle was released by Shock Entertainment in Australia and New Zealand.

It was released on DVD in Australia on May 11, 2022 with the catalogue number KAL5832 and on Blu-ray in Australia on May 11, 2022 with the catalogue number KAL5833.

 

=== ===
 was released by Roadshow Entertainment in Australian and New Zealand.

It was released on DVD in Australia on August 21, 2019 with the catalogue number R-126431-9, on Blu-ray in Australia on August 21, 2019 with the catalogue number R-125079-8, and on 4K Ultra HD Blu-Ray in Australia on August 21, 2019 with the catalogue number R-125105-8. The 4K Ultra HD Blu-Ray also came with an exclusive SteelBook release at JB Hi-FI releaseed on the same day.

 

==Multi-movie releases==
===Pokémon Movie Triple Feature===
The Pokémon Movie Triple Feature is a multi-movie DVD set released by (now known as Beyond Home Entertainment) in Australia. It contains three discs, one with Lucario and the Mystery of Mew, one with Pokémon Ranger and the Temple of the Sea, and one with The Rise of Darkrai. It was released on DVD in Australia on June 3, 2009 with the catalogue number DBX13063. This release uses a 4:3 .

 

===Pokémon Movie 4 Pack===
The Pokémon Movie 4 Pack is a multi-movie DVD set released by (now known as Beyond Home Entertainment) in Australia. It contains four discs, one with Lucario and the Mystery of Mew, one with Pokémon Ranger and the Temple of the Sea, one with The Rise of Darkrai, and one with Giratina and the Sky Warrior. This release uses a .

It was released on DVD in Australia on November 4, 2009 with the catalogue number DBX13103.

 

===Pokémon Movie 3 Pack===
The Pokémon Movie 3 Pack is a multi-movie DVD set released by (now known as Beyond Home Entertainment) in Australia. It contains four discs, one with The Rise of Darkrai, one with Giratina and the Sky Warrior, and one with Arceus and the Jewel of Life. This release uses a .

It was released on DVD in Australia on June 1, 2011 with the catalogue number DBX13695. Two different covers for the DVD were released. 

 

===Pokémon the Movie: Black & White Dual Pack===
The Pokémon the Movie: Black & White Dual Pack is a multi-movie pack released by in Australia. It contains two discs, one with Black—Victini and Reshiram and the other with White—Victini and Zekrom.

It was released on Blu-ray with the catalogue number BHE4116BR in Australia on September 5, 2012. It was released on DVD with the catalogue number BHE4115 in Australia on May 1, 2013 and in New Zealand on May 22, 2013. This release uses a .

The pair of movies was released in Limited Edition 3D packaging by Beyond Home Entertainment exclusively at stores with the catalogue number BHE7432 on November 16, 2016 in Australia. This release uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

 

===Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Movie Collection===
The Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Movie Collection is a multi-movie DVD set released by in Australia. It contains four discs, with one movie on each. It includes The Rise of Darkrai, Giratina and the Sky Warrior, Arceus and the Jewel of Life, and Zoroark: Master of Illusions. It was released on DVD in Australia on November 3, 2014 with the catalogue number BHE5783. This release uses a .

 

===Pokémon Black & White Movie Collection===
The Pokémon Black & White Movie Collection is a multi-movie DVD set released by in Australia. It contains four discs, with one movie on each. It includes White—Victini and Zekrom, Black—Victini and Reshiram, Kyurem VS. The Sword of Justice, and Genesect and The Legend Awakened. It was released on DVD in Australia on March 2, 2015 with the catalogue number BHE5784. This release uses a .

 

===Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Movie Set===
 
The Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Movie Set is a multi-movie DVD box set released by in Australia. It contains four discs, with one movie on each. It includes The Rise of Darkrai, Giratina and the Sky Warrior, Arceus and the Jewel of Life, and Zoroark: Master of Illusions. It was released on DVD in Australia on April 1, 2015 with the catalogue number BHE6195. This release uses a .

 

===Pokémon Movie Collection - Double Pack===
 
The Pokémon Movie Collection - Double Pack is a multi-movie DVD set released by in Australia and New Zealand. It contains two discs, with one movie on each. It includes Lucario and the Mystery of Mew and Pokémon Ranger and the Temple of the Sea. It was released on DVD in Australia on October 14, 2015 and in New Zealand on October 21, 2015 . 

 

===Pokémon Black & White Movie Set===
 
The Pokémon Black & White Movie Set is a multi-movie DVD box set released by in Australia. It contains four discs, with one movie on each. It includes White—Victini and Zekrom, Black—Victini and Reshiram, Kyurem VS. The Sword of Justice, and Genesect and The Legend Awakened. It was released on DVD in Australia on November 4, 2015 with the catalogue number BHE6616. This release uses a .

 

===Pokémon Movie Collection===
The Pokémon Movie Collection is a multi-movie Blu-ray set released by in Australia and New Zealand. It includes Mewtwo Strikes Back, The Power of One, and Spell of the Unown: Entei. It does not include any Pikachu shorts.

It was released on Blu-ray in a Collector's Edition Tin in Australia and New Zealand on December 2, 2015 with the catalogue number BHE6552BR. It was released on Blu-ray in a standard case in Australia on February 3, 2016 with the catalogue number BHE6682BR. These releases use a .

 

===Pokémon Diamond and Pearl: Collector's Money Tin===
The Pokémon Diamond and Pearl: Collector's Money Tin is a multi-movie DVD tin released by in Australia. It contains four discs, with one movie on each. It includes The Rise of Darkrai, Giratina and the Sky Warrior, Arceus and the Jewel of Life, and Zoroark: Master of Illusions. It was released on DVD in Australia on November 18, 2015 with the catalogue number BHE6543. This release uses a .

The outer packaging also serves as a . Inside, it includes two DVD cases branded as Double Packs: one containing The Rise of Darkrai and Giratina and the Sky Warrior, the other containing Arceus and the Jewel of Life and Zoroark: Master of Illusions.

 

===Pokémon: Movies 1-3 Gold Edition===
Pokémon: Movies 1-3 Gold Edition is a multi-movie set released on DVD and Blu-ray in Australia and New Zealand by . It includes the first three Pokémon movies (Mewtwo Strikes Back, The Power of One, and Spell of the Unown: Entei) and their corresponding Pikachu shorts (Pikachu's Vacation, Pikachu's Rescue Adventure, and Pikachu & Pichu). It contains four discs. This release uses a , except for Pikachu's Vacation which uses a 4:3 aspect ratio.

It was released on DVD in Australia and New Zealand on July 5, 2017 with the catalogue number BHE7651. It was released on Blu-ray exclusively at .

 

===Pokémon XY Movie Collection===
The Pokémon XY Movie Collection is a multi-movie DVD set released by in Australia and New Zealand. It contains three discs, with one movie on each. It includes Diancie and the Cocoon of Destruction, Hoopa and the Clash of Ages, and Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel. It was released in Australia on June 6, 2018 and in New Zealand on June 20, 2018 with the catalogue number BHE7862. This release uses a .

 

===Pokémon: Movies 1-3 Collection===
 
Pokémon: Movies 1-3 Collection is a multi-movie DVD set released by in Australia on December 5, 2019 and New Zealand on December 12, 2019 with the catalogue number BHE8023. It includes the first three Pokémon movies (Mewtwo Strikes Back, The Power of One, and Spell of the Unown: Entei) and their corresponding Pikachu shorts (Pikachu's Vacation, Pikachu's Rescue Adventure, and Pikachu & Pichu). It contains four discs. 

 

===Pokémon: Movie Double Pack: I Choose You & The Power of Us===
The Pokémon: Movie Double Pack: I Choose You & The Power of Us is a multi-movie DVD set released by in Australia and New Zealand. It contains two discs, containing I Choose You! and The Power of Us, respectively.

It was released on DVD in Australia on December 5, 2018 and in New Zealand on December 12, 2018 with the catalogue number BHE8079. This release uses a .

It was released on Blu-ray in Australia on April 3, 2019 and in New Zealand on May 22, 2019 with the catalogue number BHE8137BR. 

 

===Pokémon - Movies 1-3 Collectors Edition===
The Pokémon - Movies 1-3 Collectors Edition is a multi-movie set released by Shock Entertainment consisting of the first three Pokémon movies (Mewtwo Strikes Back, The Power of One, and Spell of the Unown: Entei) and their corresponding Pikachu shorts (Pikachu's Vacation, Pikachu's Rescue Adventure, and Pikachu & Pichu)

It was released on DVD in Australia on December 12, 2020 and in New Zealand on January 27, 2021 with the catalogue number KAL5446 and on Blu-ray in Australia on December 12, 2020 and in New Zealand on January 27, 2021 with the catalogue number KAL5447.

This is the first Pokémon home video release by Shock Entertainment, following Beyond Home Entertainment's exit out of the Home Media industry in August 2020.

 

===Pokémon - Movie Triple Pack===
The Pokémon - Movie Triple Pack is a multi-movie DVD set released by Shock Entertainment consisting of I Choose You!, The Power of Us and Mewtwo Strikes Back—Evolution.

It was released in Australia on March 3, 2021 and in New Zealand on May 19, 2021 with the catalogue number KAL5445B.

sections.heading: Mewtwo Strikes Back
sections.text:
Pokémon: The First Movie - Mewtwo Strikes Back was initially released on home video in Australia by Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Pikachu's Vacation. The promotional card was included in early releases of the DVD. It was released on VHS in Australia with the catalogue number 18270. It was released on DVD in Australia with the catalogue number DVS18270. These releases use a 4:3 .

The DVD has English, French, Italian, Dutch, and Portuguese audio; with optional English, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, English for the hearing impaired, and Italian for the hearing impaired closed captions. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Commentary audio track by Director Michael Haigney and Producer Norman J. Grossfeld
The Story of Mewtwo's Origin (first two minutes of The Uncut Story of Mewtwo's Origin)
Music video for 's " " (the movie's ending theme)
Theatrical trailer of the movie
Preview of The Power of One
"Ash's Journey"
DVD-ROM features 

The VHS had The Story of Mewtwo's Origin (first two minutes of The Uncut Story of Mewtwo's Origin) added to the beginning of the film.

It was re-released on DVD in a Collector's Edition Tin in Australia and New Zealand by on December 2, 2015 with the catalogue number BHE6417. It was released on DVD in standard case by Beyond Home Entertainment in Australia on February 3, 2016 and in New Zealand on February 17, 2016 with the catalogue number BHE6679. These releases do not include a Pikachu short or any other special features. These releases use a .

It was re-released once again by Shock Entertainment in Australia on February 3, 2021 and in New Zealand on March 24, 2021 with an updated cover and the catalogue number KAL5556B.
